boundary: This IDENTIFIES two known bounds as one number; it derives no new bound and neither route is original. The embedding is the standard eigenspace projection, checked equal-norm and two-distance by assertion at each q. The closing paragraph about two-distance bounds using BOTH inner products is a DIRECTION, not a result -- no such bound is constructed or shown to exist

pass_5278.frame_bound: unit vectors at constant inner product c<0 satisfy N <= 1 - 1/c, from Gram positive-semidefiniteness
pass_5278.source: Track B Pass5261: 156 minimum footprint words form an equal-norm two-distance tight frame in R^90, inner products 2/15 collinear and -1/25 noncollinear
pass_5278.why_they_meet: a coclique uses only the noncollinear value, so a two-distance frame restricted to a coclique is a one-distance set

pass_5279.open_direction: a bound using BOTH inner products would see the geometry; not constructed here
pass_5279.reading: the frame route explains what the bound MEANS -- q^2+1 unit vectors at constant angle is all that fits -- and also why it cannot see existence: Gram PSD constrains how many fit, not whether the geometry realises them
